title: Mortara wins at the Red Bull Ring as Green's gearshift hands Wehrlein the lead
dek: Edoardo Mortara converted pole into victory for Audi Sport Team Abt, 1.792 seconds clear of Pascal Wehrlein, after Jamie Green's gearshift failed while leading and Wehrlein took over the championship.

chapters.title: Halfway through a tight championship
text: The DTM reached the halfway point of its 2015 season at the Red Bull Ring in Spielberg on 1–2 August: the fifth of nine weekends, in a season in which every weekend carried two races. Jamie Green arrived at the head of the table for Audi Sport Team Rosberg on 81 points, but the lead was anything but safe, with Pascal Wehrlein and Mattias Ekström both on 76, Edoardo Mortara on 58, Robert Wickens on 57 and Bruno Spengler on 52. Green had also left the previous round at Zandvoort without a point, in a weekend that had belonged to BMW: Marco Wittmann won Saturday's race and António Félix da Costa took Sunday's from pole.

Austria threatened BMW with a hard landing. In the second free practice session on Saturday morning Mortara was quickest again for Audi Sport Team Abt, with Green 0.066 seconds behind and Wehrlein, the best of the Mercedes-AMG drivers, 0.151 off the pace. Wittmann, ninth, was the only BMW in the top ten, and the rest of the marque's cars finished the session more than seven tenths away from the front. Wehrlein's own weekend had started awkwardly: damage to his car in Friday's session left him with only about ten minutes of running, and his mechanics rebuilt it overnight. Local interest centred on Lucas Auer, the Austrian, making his home appearance in the Euronics/BWT Mercedes-AMG.

chapters.title: Audi takes the front row back from Mercedes
text: Mercedes-AMG set the early marker in the 20-minute session, with Wehrlein and Paul di Resta holding the front row for much of it. Midway through, Miguel Molina stopped his Audi with a failure at Turn 6, which brought out a red flag; the session resumed with 8:15 left on the clock, and the stranded car meant Molina could only qualify 20th.

When the track opened up again the Audis moved. Mortara, who had led both practice sessions, lapped in 1:24.714 to take pole, and Green, whose best time came only in the closing stages, was 0.193 seconds slower in second to make it an Audi front row. Wehrlein was third on 1:24.926 as the leading Mercedes, with di Resta fourth. Augusto Farfus, fifth for BMW Team RBM, was the only BMW in the top ten; Christian Vietoris, Wickens and Gary Paffett made it five Mercedes among the first eight, and Ekström and Mike Rockenfeller were ninth and tenth. Adrien Tambay missed the top ten by 0.078 seconds.

Elsewhere on BMW's side of the grid it was a poor session. Wittmann was 12th, Félix da Costa 13th and Spengler 15th, while Martin Tomczyk, Maxime Martin, Tom Blomqvist and Timo Glock were 18th, 19th, 21st and 23rd. Auer, in front of his home crowd, shared the last row with Glock in 24th.

chapters.title: Green leads, then loses his gears
text: Mortara had the pace but not the start. Green got away better from second and led into Turn 1, with Wehrlein third and di Resta fourth. The lead did not last: Green's Audi stuck in gear and he was out within the first three laps, having said the upshift stopped working on the exit of the last corner and the car then would not downshift for Turn 1. Mortara was back in front on lap two.

It was the fourth race in a row in which Green failed to score, and with it went his place at the top of the standings. Behind Mortara the Mercedes pair of Wehrlein and di Resta settled into second and third and set off after the Audi. Wickens, seventh on the grid, was out after seven laps and Tomczyk's BMW followed after ten, so that each of the three manufacturers had lost exactly one car before half distance.

chapters.title: Fighting for the last points
text: The racing was in the middle of the order. Ekström, ninth on the grid, worked his way forward by outbraking Paffett's Mercedes and was in the fight for fifth with Farfus and Vietoris for most of the race. Vietoris, who had started sixth, held fourth place.

Further back, Rockenfeller, Wittmann and Tambay swapped positions repeatedly over the places that carried the final points. Rockenfeller finished eighth, Wittmann ninth and Tambay took the last point in tenth, while Paffett kept seventh.

chapters.title: Mortara wins by 1.792 seconds
text: Once Green was out Mortara had the race under control. He took the flag after 29 laps in 41:41.536, 1.792 seconds ahead of Wehrlein, and also set the fastest lap of the race, a 1:25.632 on lap 10. Wehrlein admitted that Green's retirement had helped him. Di Resta was a distant third, 11.200 seconds behind the winner, with Vietoris fourth after another seven seconds, which gave Mercedes three of the first four places.

The last lap decided fifth place. Ekström, who had been closing on Farfus for the final two or three laps, went past the BMW to claim it, 19.300 seconds behind Mortara; Farfus was sixth, and Wittmann's ninth made him the only other BMW driver in the points.

The result reshuffled the title fight. Wehrlein took the lead of the championship with 94 points, becoming the youngest driver to head the standings, ahead of Ekström on 86, Mortara on 83 and Green, who fell from first to fourth on 81.

facts.v: Jamie Green led from the start, but his Audi's gearshift stopped working and he was out within three laps, his fourth race in a row without points.
